aq.precedente: Has it been tried before, and did it work?
aq.impacto: What does this change, and for whom?

guard.apoio_em_fatos: Every claim points to a fact
guard.magnitude_com_base: Impact size only with numbers from the facts
num.no_average: When sources disagree, Polarized shows every version. There is no average.
sev.fixed_rule: The rule is the same for every case of this type and lives in the project's open code. Nobody assigns the score by hand.
f.no_point: no point on the map — affects systems worldwide
attr.program_unknown: program not yet described by the project
x.intensity: Severity is a 0–5 score that Polarized calculates with a fixed rule from the source's numbers (deaths, magnitude, reach, length of a list). It lets the map compare very different things. It is nobody's opinion.
x.confidence: How confident we are that the record is correct, from 0 to 100%. It rises with primary sources and independent sources that agree; it falls with isolated reports.
x.condition: A situation that lasts: a war, a sanctions regime, an election period. It has a start and may not have ended.
x.event: Something that happened on a date: an earthquake, an attack, a debate.
x.observed: When the source recorded or published the data. It can differ from when the fact began.
x.sources: How many independent sources carry this fact. The full list, with links, is under "Where it comes from".
x.versions: Different sources published different numbers. Polarized shows every version side by side instead of picking one or averaging them.
x.analysis: A reading made by AI from the facts in the snapshot, always kept apart from them. Every claim points to the fact behind it, and the code discards analyses that give percentage odds, give investment advice or claim things without support.
x.market: The AI looks in the collected facts for what may have weighed on each day. Happening at the same time does not prove cause. It never forecasts prices or advises investing.
x.attention: A number from 0 to 100 summarizing how much is happening in the country now, compared with the country getting the most attention. Severity weighs more than volume.
x.corroboration: How many different newsrooms, from how many countries, told the same story. One newsroom does not confirm; several independent ones confirm more.
x.coverage: Which regions and types of outlets the news about this country comes from. Coverage entirely from abroad, or from a single type of outlet, is a lens.
x.program: Each sanctions list is split into programs created by a law, executive order or resolution. The program says why the person or company was sanctioned.
x.status.nao_verificado: Comes from a single source, not yet independently confirmed.
x.status.corroborado: Two or more independent sources say the same.
x.status.verificado: Comes from a primary source (the body that measures or decides).
x.status.disputado: Sources disagree on something important. See the versions.
x.rel.sanciona: The first country or bloc keeps sanctions on the second: frozen assets, business or travel bans.
x.rel.conflito_com: The two governments have been in recorded armed conflict in recent months.
x.rel.acordo_com: The two have a recorded agreement.
x.designation: A designation is a name on the sanctions list: a person, company, ship or aircraft. Those on the list have their assets frozen and cannot do business with anyone bound by the sanctioning party's rules.
disp.title: Disputed territory
disp.policy: Polarized uses the name adopted by the UN and shows what each party calls the place. Marking it as disputed is not taking sides.
trk.heading: Heading
trk.delay_p: This track crosses an active conflict zone. Project policy only publishes military positions from these zones after the delay, so as not to expose ongoing operations.
trk.why_p: Rule: {rule} · confidence {n}%. ADS-B and AIS do not say whether a vehicle is military; the classification is an open heuristic of the project. Military craft that switch off their transponders do not appear, so absence on the map is not absence in the world.

cov.home.one: {n} from an outlet based in the country.
cov.home.other: {n} from outlets based in the country.

cov.no_home: None from outlets based in the country.
cov.lens: Coverage that comes entirely from abroad, or entirely from one type of outlet, is a lens — read it knowing that.
att.label: Attention index
att.sub: 0 to 100, relative to the country with the most attention now
att.formula: For each country and layer: the most severe fact counts in full and the rest add with diminishing returns (half the square root of their sum), so severity weighs more than volume. Each fact is worth its severity times the layer weight (conflict 1; earthquakes and climate 0.8; protests 0.7; cyber 0.6; diplomacy, elections and economy 0.5; military 0.3), and events lose half their weight every 33 hours. News adds 0.15 each, up to 3 points; a strong stock market move, up to 1. The index runs from 0 to 100 relative to the country with the most attention now.

about.lang_p: The interface is translated by hand. Headlines, summaries and analyses are machine-translated, with numbers and dates checked; the original is always one tap away.
about.h1: One planet, read all at once
about.intro: Polarized shows the state of the world on a single globe. Each symbol is a place where something is happening now: war, election, protest, tariff, embargo, earthquake, internet outage, military aircraft or ship. You spin, tap and read.
about.symbols_p: Each layer has its own color and frame, and each kind of event has an icon. Shape and color say the same thing, so the map also works for people who cannot tell colors apart. Zoom into the globe (pinch or mouse wheel) to see the events inside each conflict.
about.ai_p: The most important facts get an analysis: what has been tried in history and how it ended, what changes and for whom, whether a statement holds up, why a market moved. The analysis is never mixed with the fact — it is labeled, with its reasoning in view. Before it appears, the code checks:
about.g1: Every claim points to a fact on the list. Anything unsupported is removed.
about.g2: No percentage odds. Instead, the conditions that mattered in history and whether they are present here.
about.g3: There is always a counterargument: the strongest case against the conclusion.
about.g4: Impact size only appears when the facts carry the number.
about.g5: Historical cases appear as unverified until a person reviews them.
about.g6: No investment advice and no price forecasts, in any language.
about.g7: When a second model is configured, the two analyses are compared and any disagreement is shown.
about.ai_after: An analysis that fails one of these rules is discarded, not quietly fixed.
about.news_p: The News tab groups headlines from different outlets about the same fact and shows how many newsrooms, from how many countries, told the story. A single newsroom confirms nothing. State-funded outlets are labeled. Polarized keeps only the headline, link and the outlet's own summary.
about.markets_p: The Markets tab has stock indices, currencies and commodities at daily close. The AI explains day by day what in the collected facts may have moved each series — always noting that correlation is not causation, without forecasting prices or giving investment advice. When the facts do not explain a day, it says so.
about.country_p: Tap a country to zoom in: you get its states, the attention index, an overview, its links with other countries and where the coverage comes from.
about.tr_p: Content is written in Portuguese and translated by AI into each language. Before publishing, the code checks that every number and date in the original is in the translation; anything that fails stays in the original, labeled. Outlet headlines are never rewritten: you see the original and the translation below it.
about.fund_p: Discreet ads inside the feed — never over the globe, never interrupting reading — and donations from users. The ad space is marked in the list to show where it goes.
about.support_note: Payments are not connected in this prototype yet. When they are, this button opens the support page.
about.oss_p: The globe, source adapters, editorial policy and analysis safeguards are public for anyone to audit, fix or run themselves. AGPL-3.0 license: anyone who publishes a modified version must also open its code.
about.credits: Country and state outlines: Natural Earth (public domain), via world-atlas.
